description: What if there were no rules? Mayor Robo tries a No-Rules Day in Toy Town and it's a silly muddle! Learn why rules keep us safe, fair and kind, how to cross the street with a grown-up, what good citizens do, and how a group votes. Frog loses the vote like a good sport.

youtube.title: Rules and Good Citizens for Kids! Toy Town Votes | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
What if there were no rules? Mayor Robo tries a No-Rules Day in Toy Town and it's a silly muddle! Learn why rules keep us safe, fair and kind, how to cross the street with a grown-up, what good citizens do, and how a group votes. Frog loses the vote like a good sport.
For first graders. Practise crossing the street only with a grown-up holding your hand.

do.text: Hello! Today I'm Mayor for a Day of Toy Town!
What if there were no rules? Let's try it!
It's No-Rules Day!
Oh my! Everyone talks at the same time!
Balls bounce everywhere!
Everyone goes down the slide at once. A big pile!
And the bin tipped over! What a silly muddle.
Nobody is hurt. But this is no fun!
Hmm. Maybe rules are a good idea!
A rule tells us what to do. Here is our rules board.
rule
Rules keep us safe.
safe
Rules keep things fair.
fair
And rules help us be kind.
kind
Let's try the slide again, with a rule: one at a time.
Wheee! One at a time is more fun!
It works! Everyone gets a turn, and nobody bumps.
Rules keep us...
Safe, fair and kind! Stomp, stomp, stomp!
That's how our town works!
Rules are at home, at school and in town.
At home: put your toys away.
I'll tidy up!
At school: raise your hand to talk.
In the library: use a quiet voice.
We use quiet voices so everyone can read.
New rule! Everyone must hop everywhere!
Shh, Frog! Not here.
Oops. Sorry, Sheep.
Fun fact: many libraries let you borrow books for free!
In town: put litter in the bin.
Rules help everywhere we go!
Dog is our crossing guard. Let's cross the street!
Hold a grown-up's hand. Stop at the edge.
stop
Look both ways, and listen.
look
listen
Hands up to stop. Turn your head. Hand to your ear!
Here's the traffic light. Red means stop.
Yellow means slow down.
Green means go.
Wait for the green walking signal.
Then cross together, and keep looking as you go.
We made it safely!
Fun fact: the first traffic light was in London, long ago.
Stop, look, listen! That's how we cross.
A citizen is a person who belongs to a town.
citizen
Good citizens help, share, take turns and clean up.
good citizen
Show me a thumbs up for a good choice!
Cow carries a heavy bag for Duck.
help
Thumbs up! A good choice.
Bunny and Sheep share a ball.
share
Thumbs up! A good choice.
Uh-oh. Frog drops litter on the grass.
Thumbs down! That's not a good choice.
You're right. I'll put it in the bin!
Everyone helps clean up the park.
clean up
Duck waters the flowers to care for the park.
Thumbs up! A good choice.
Helping, sharing and caring make a good community!
community
Now, we need a new playground rule. Let's vote!
vote
A vote is how a group chooses together.
My idea: everyone must hop everywhere!
My idea: take turns on the slide.
Each friend hops once to vote. Which rule will win?
And Frog votes for hop everywhere. 1!
Take turns has 5 votes. Hop everywhere has 1.
5 to 1
Take turns wins!
That's fair. Five is more than one.
And I can still hop at playtime!
Frog is a good sport. That's a good citizen too!
Fun fact: in many places, grown-ups vote in secret.
Citizen quiz! Think, then shout.
Citizen Quiz
Question one. Why do we have rules?
To keep us safe, to be fair and to be kind!
Question two. Name a library rule.
Use a quiet voice!
Question three. What do you do before crossing the street?
Hold a grown-up's hand. Stop, look both ways and listen!
Question four. Duck sees litter in the park. What should Duck do?
Put it in the bin, or tell a grown-up!
Last one. Take turns got 5 votes. Hop everywhere got 1.
Which rule won?
Take turns!
Our new rule goes on the board. Take turns!
Playtime! Hop, hop, hop!
Rules keep us safe, fair and kind.
And good citizens help their town. Good citizens!
GOOD CITIZENS!
Bye-bye from Toy Town!
